title: מַסֶּכֶת אָבוֹת — פֶּרֶק רְבִיעִי
part: Chapter 4 · Ben Zoma to "Those who are born are to die"
draftNote: The text follows the Wikisource transcription of the Kaufmann manuscript, apart from the editorial steps named in the source note; the prepared audio is being recorded; a check against the manuscript photographs is still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any mishnah to report a problem.
source: Text: the Kaufmann manuscript of the Mishnah (Budapest, Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Kaufmann A 50), fols. 169r–173v, from the diplomatic transcription on Hebrew Wikisource (כתב יד קאופמן למשנה/מסכת אבות, CC BY-SA 4.0), which records the work of the later hands. The vowel points are the manuscript's own. Where it leaves a letter of a pointed word bare, the editor has supplied the point, and the mishnah's note lists every such word; words the manuscript leaves wholly unpointed stay unpointed. Reading text: the manuscript as corrected. Letters the manuscript erases are omitted; corrections and additions by later hands, including marginal ones, are printed; marginal variant readings (נ״א) are left out. Words the scribe broke across a line end are rejoined. The scribe's abbreviations are kept, marked with a geresh (׳), and expanded in the glossary. The transcription writes Kaufmann's ḥolam, which sits over the preceding letter, as a dot on that letter; it is given here as an ordinary ḥolam. Mishnayot are numbered as in the standard printed editions; where Kaufmann divides differently, or lacks a mishnah, the note says so. Romanization: simplified, following Modern Israeli pronunciation. Pronunciation convention: Modern Israeli Hebrew applied to Kaufmann's vowels — an admitted choice, since the manuscript's pointing reflects an older Palestinian tradition. Translations made fresh from the Hebrew and Aramaic; no modern translation consulted. Audio: Google Cloud TTS, Modern Israeli Hebrew voice, reading the pointed text; abbreviations are read in full (או׳ as אוֹמֵר, שנ׳ as שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, the divine name as Adonay).
about: Avot, "Fathers", is the tractate of the Mishnah made up of maxims; the rest of the Mishnah is law. It opens with the chain of tradition from Moses at Sinai to the Men of the Great Assembly, then gives the sayings of the sages from the early pairs down to the generation of the Mishnah's editor, Rabbi Judah the Prince. The Mishnah was compiled around 200 CE. Many communities read Avot a chapter at a time on Sabbath afternoons between Passover and Shavuot, and often through the summer, adding a sixth chapter, Kinyan Torah, to make six weeks. Chapters 1–5 here follow a single manuscript, the Kaufmann codex, probably copied in Italy in the eleventh or twelfth century and the best witness to the Mishnah's own Hebrew. It reads differently from the familiar printed text in many small places, and the notes point them out.

sentences.t: בֶּן זוֹמָה אוֹמֵ׳ אֵי זֶה הוּא חָכָם הַלָּמֵד מִכָּל אָדָם שֶׁנ׳ מִכָּל מְלַמְּדַי הִשְׂכַּלְתִּי אֵיזֶה הוּא גִּיבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ שֶׁנ׳ טוֹב אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם מִגִּבּוֹר וּמוֹשֵׁל בְּרוּחוֹ מִלֹּכֶד עִיר אֵי זֶה הוּא עָשִׁיר הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ שנ׳ יְגִיעַ כַּפֶּיךָ כִּי תֹאכֵל אַשְׁרֶיךָ וְטוֹב לָךְ אֵיזֶה הוּא מְכוּבָּד הַמְכַבֵּד אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת שנ׳ כִּי מְכַבְּדַי אֲכַבֵּד וּבֹזַיִ יקלו:
sentences.tr: Ben Zoma omer: ei ze hu ḥakham? Ha-lamed mi-kol adam, she-ne'emar: mi-kol melamdai hiskalti. Eize hu gibor? Ha-kovesh et yitsro, she-ne'emar: tov erekh apayim mi-gibor, u-moshel be-ruḥo mi-lokhed ir. Ei ze hu ashir? Ha-same'aḥ be-ḥelko, she-ne'emar: yegi'a kapekha ki tokhel, ashrekha ve-tov lakh. Eize hu mekhubad? Ha-mekhabed et ha-briyot, she-ne'emar: ki mekhabdai akhabed, u-vozai yekalu.
sentences.l: Ben Zoma says: which is he (that is) wise? The one-who-learns from every person, as it is said: from all my teachers I gained-understanding. Which is he (that is) mighty? The one-who-subdues his inclination, as it is said: better slow of anger than a mighty-man, and one-who-rules his spirit than one-who-captures a city. Which is he (that is) rich? The one-who-rejoices in his portion, as it is said: the toil of your hands when you eat (it), happy are you and good for you. Which is he (that is) honoured? The one-who-honours the creatures, as it is said: for those-who-honour-Me I will honour, and those-who-despise-Me will be-made-light.
sentences.i: Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from everyone, as it is said, 'From all my teachers I have gained understanding' (Psalm 119:99). Who is mighty? One who masters his impulse, as it is said, 'Better to be slow to anger than a warrior, and to rule one's own spirit than to take a city' (Proverbs 16:32). Who is rich? One who is content with his lot, as it is said, 'When you eat from the toil of your hands, you are happy and it is well with you' (Psalm 128:2). Who is honoured? One who honours others, as it is said, 'Those who honour Me I will honour, and those who scorn Me shall be held in contempt' (1 Samuel 2:30).
sentences.n: Shimon ben Zoma, an early second-century sage, is always called by his father's name. אֵי זֶה הוּא, 'which is he', is the Mishnah's way of asking for a definition, and each answer turns the expected quality around: the wise man is the one still learning, the strong man the one who holds himself back. יֵצֶר, 'inclination', is the rabbinic word for a person's drive, especially toward wrongdoing. The last verse speaks of God's own honour; Ben Zoma applies it to how people treat one another (בְּרִיּוֹת, 'creatures', = people). Its last two words are only partly vocalized: יקלו (yekallu) has no points at all. The printed editions follow the Psalm verse with a gloss — 'happy are you in this world, and it will be well with you in the world to come'; Kaufmann has the verse alone. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: שֶׁנ׳, תֹאכֵל.
sentences.say: בֶּן זוֹמָה אוֹמֵר אֵי זֶה הוּא חָכָם הַלָּמֵד מִכָּל אָדָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר מִכָּל מְלַמְּדַי הִשְׂכַּלְתִּי אֵיזֶה הוּא גִּיבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר טוֹב אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם מִגִּבּוֹר וּמוֹשֵׁל בְּרוּחוֹ מִלֹּכֶד עִיר אֵי זֶה הוּא עָשִׁיר הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יְגִיעַ כַּפֶּיךָ כִּי תֹאכֵל אַשְׁרֶיךָ וְטוֹב לָךְ אֵיזֶה הוּא מְכוּבָּד הַמְכַבֵּד אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי מְכַבְּדַי אֲכַבֵּד וּבֹזַיִ יקלו:

sentences.t: בֶּן עַזַּיִי אוֹמֵ׳ הֱוֵי רָץ לְמִצְוָה קַלָּה וּבוֹרֵחַ מִן הַעֲבֵירָה שֶׁמִּצְוָה גוֹרֶרֶת מִצְוָה וַעֲבֵירָה גוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה שְׁשְׂכַר מִצְוָה מִצְוָה וּשְׂכַר עֲבֵירָה עֲבֵירָה
sentences.tr: Ben Azay omer: hevei rats le-mitsva kala, u-vore'aḥ min ha-avera, she-mitsva goreret mitsva, va-avera goreret avera, she-skhar mitsva mitsva, u-skhar avera avera.
sentences.l: Ben Azzai says: be running to a light commandment, and fleeing from the transgression; for a commandment drags (along) a commandment, and a transgression drags (along) a transgression; for the reward of a commandment (is) a commandment, and the reward of a transgression (is) a transgression.
sentences.i: Ben Azzai says: Run to do even a minor commandment, and flee from transgression. One commandment brings another in its wake, and one transgression brings another; the reward for a commandment is a commandment, and the reward for a transgression is a transgression.
sentences.n: Shimon ben Azzai was Ben Zoma's contemporary and fellow student. מִצְוָה is a commandment, and by extension the good deed of fulfilling one; עֲבֵירָה, literally 'a crossing over', is a transgression. The second שֶׁ- gives the reason for the first: the deed is its own payment, since it leads to the next one. The printed editions add כְּבַחֲמוּרָה, 'as to a weighty one', after 'a light commandment'; Kaufmann lacks the words. Kaufmann puts a shva under the prefix of שְׁשְׂכַר. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: מִצְוָה.
sentences.say: בֶּן עַזַּיִי אוֹמֵר הֱוֵי רָץ לְמִצְוָה קַלָּה וּבוֹרֵחַ מִן הַעֲבֵירָה שֶׁמִּצְוָה גוֹרֶרֶת מִצְוָה וַעֲבֵירָה גוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה שְׁשְׂכַר מִצְוָה מִצְוָה וּשְׂכַר עֲבֵירָה עֲבֵירָה

sentences.t: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵ׳ אַל תְהִי בָז לְכָל אָדָם וְאַל תְּהִי מַפְלִיג לְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לָךְ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה וְאֵין לָךְ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם
sentences.tr: Hu haya omer: al tehi vaz le-khol adam, ve-al tehi maflig le-khol davar, she-ein lakh adam she-ein lo sha'a, ve-ein lakh davar she-ein lo makom.
sentences.l: He was saying: do not be scornful to any person, and do not be dismissive to any thing; for there is not for-you a person who has not an hour, and there is not for-you a thing that has not a place.
sentences.i: He used to say: Do not scorn anyone, and do not dismiss anything as far-fetched. Every person has his hour, and every thing has its place.
sentences.n: 'He' is Ben Azzai. מַפְלִיג, from הִפְלִיג 'to set far off', means dismissing something as remote or impossible. שֶׁאֵין לָךְ …, literally 'there is not for you …', is the Mishnaic idiom for 'there is no …'. In Kaufmann a mem was erased before שָׁעָה.
sentences.say: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר אַל תְהִי בָז לְכָל אָדָם וְאַל תְּהִי מַפְלִיג לְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לָךְ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה וְאֵין לָךְ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם

sentences.t: רְ׳ לְוִייטַס אִישׁ יַבְנֶה אוֹ׳ מְאֹד מְאֹד הֱוֵי שְׁפַל רוּחַ שֶׁתִּקְוַת אֱנוֹשׁ רִימָּה: ר׳ יוֹחָנַן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹ׳ כָּל הַמְחַלֵּל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בַּסֵּתֶר נִפְרָעִים מִמֶּנּוּ בַגָּלוּי אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג ואֶחָד מֵזִיד בְּחִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם.
sentences.tr: Rabi Levitas ish Yavne omer: me'od me'od hevei shfal ruaḥ, she-tikvat enosh rima. Rabi Yoḥanan ben Beroka omer: kol ha-meḥalel shem shamayim ba-seter nifra'im mimenu ba-galuy, eḥad shogeg ve-eḥad mezid be-ḥilul ha-shem.
sentences.l: Rabbi Levitas man of Yavne says: very very be low of spirit, for the hope of man (is) the worm. Rabbi Yoḥanan son of Beroka says: whoever profanes the name of Heaven in secret, they exact-payment from him in the open; one (who is) inadvertent and one (who is) deliberate (are alike) in profanation of the Name.
sentences.i: Rabbi Levitas of Yavne says: Be exceedingly humble, for what awaits a human being is the worm. Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says: Whoever profanes the name of Heaven in secret is punished in public. In profaning the Name, the unwitting and the wilful are alike.
sentences.n: Yavne, on the coastal plain, is where the sages regrouped after the Temple fell in 70 CE. אֱנוֹשׁ רִמָּה, 'man is a worm', comes from Job 25:6; in Levitas's sentence the worm is the one that waits in the grave. נִפְרָעִים, 'they exact payment', is an impersonal plural, the Mishnah's reverent way of saying that God punishes. שׁוֹגֵג and מֵזִיד are the legal terms for an unintentional and an intentional offender. Manuscript: the בַ of בַגָּלוּי was corrected from כ, and the vav of ואֶחָד was added by a second hand and left unpointed. Kaufmann begins a new section at R. Yoḥanan ben Beroka.
sentences.say: רַבִּי לְוִייטַס אִישׁ יַבְנֶה אוֹמֵר מְאֹד מְאֹד הֱוֵי שְׁפַל רוּחַ שֶׁתִּקְוַת אֱנוֹשׁ רִימָּה: רַבִּי יוֹחָנַן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר כָּל הַמְחַלֵּל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בַּסֵּתֶר נִפְרָעִים מִמֶּנּוּ בַגָּלוּי אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג ואֶחָד מֵזִיד בְּחִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם.

sentences.t: ר׳ יִשְׁמָעֵא׳ אוֹ׳ הַלָּמֵד עַל מְנַת לְלַמֵּד מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לִלְמוֹד וּלְלַמֵּד הַלָּמֵד עַל מְנַת לַעֲשׂוֹת מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לִלְמוֹד וּלְלַמֵּד לִשְׁמוֹר וְלַעֲשׂוֹת: ר׳ צָדוֹק אוֹ׳ אַל תַּעֲשֵׂם עֲטָרָה לְהִתְגַּדֵּל בָּהֶן וְלֹא קוֹרְדּוֹם לֹאכַל מֵהֶן וְכָךְ הָיָה הֶלֵּל אוֹ׳ וְדִיִשְׁתַּמָּשׁ בְּתָגָא חָלַף הָאכָּל הַנֵּאוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נָטַל חַיָּיו מִן הָעוֹלָם:
sentences.tr: Rabi Yishma'el omer: ha-lamed al menat lelamed maspikin be-yado lilmod u-lelamed; ha-lamed al menat la'asot maspikin be-yado lilmod u-lelamed, lishmor ve-la'asot. Rabi Tsadok omer: al ta'asem atara le-hitgadel bahen, ve-lo kordom lokhal mehen. Ve-khakh haya Helel omer: ve-di-yishtamash be-taga ḥalaf. Ha kol ha-ne'ot mi-divrei tora natal ḥayav min ha-olam.
sentences.l: Rabbi Ishmael says: the one-who-learns in order to teach, they supply in his hand to learn and to teach; the one-who-learns in order to do, they supply in his hand to learn and to teach, to keep and to do. Rabbi Tsadok says: do not make-them a crown to make-yourself-great with them, and not an axe to eat from them. And thus Hillel was saying: and who makes-use of the crown passes-away. Lo, whoever benefits from words of Torah has taken his life from the world.
sentences.i: Rabbi Ishmael says: One who learns in order to teach is given the means to learn and to teach. One who learns in order to practise is given the means to learn and to teach, to observe and to practise. Rabbi Tsadok says: Do not make the words of Torah a crown to exalt yourself with, or an axe to make your living by. Hillel used to say the same: Whoever makes use of the crown passes away. So whoever profits from the words of Torah takes his own life out of the world.
sentences.n: מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ, 'they supply into his hand', is another impersonal plural: Heaven gives him the means. In R. Tsadok's saying 'them' are the words of Torah, named only at the end; a קַרְדֹּם is a workman's axe or spade — Torah used as a trade. Hillel's Aramaic line already appeared at 1:13. Manuscript: the scribe first wrote אֵין before the first מַסְפִּיקִין ('he is not given the means') and erased it; a stray וְלַעֲשׂוֹת after the first clause was also erased; לִשְׁמוֹר was added in the margin, and the vav of וְדִי by a second hand. The last sentence first read הָאוֹכֵל הַנֵּאוֹת, 'one who eats the benefits', and was corrected to הָא כָּל, 'lo, whoever'. The printed editions read 'a spade to dig with' (לַחְפֹּר בָּהֶם) and 'hence you learn: whoever benefits (הַנֶּהֱנֶה)'. Kaufmann begins a new section at R. Tsadok.
sentences.say: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר הַלָּמֵד עַל מְנַת לְלַמֵּד מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לִלְמוֹד וּלְלַמֵּד הַלָּמֵד עַל מְנַת לַעֲשׂוֹת מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לִלְמוֹד וּלְלַמֵּד לִשְׁמוֹר וְלַעֲשׂוֹת: רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר אַל תַּעֲשֵׂם עֲטָרָה לְהִתְגַּדֵּל בָּהֶן וְלֹא קוֹרְדּוֹם לֹאכַל מֵהֶן וְכָךְ הָיָה הֶלֵּל אוֹמֵר וְדִיִשְׁתַּמָּשׁ בְּתָגָא חָלַף הָאכָּל הַנֵּאוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נָטַל חַיָּיו מִן הָעוֹלָם:

sentences.t: ר׳ יוֹסֵה אוֹמֵ׳ כָּל הַמְכַבֵּד אֶת הַתּוֹרָה גוּפוֹ מְכוּבַּד מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת וְכָל הַמְחַלֵּל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה גוּפוֹ מְחוּלָּל מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת:
sentences.tr: Rabi Yose omer: kol ha-mekhabed et ha-tora gufo mekhubad min ha-briyot, ve-khol ha-meḥalel et ha-tora gufo meḥulal min ha-briyot.
sentences.l: Rabbi Yose says: whoever honours the Torah, his body is honoured by the creatures; and whoever profanes the Torah, his body is profaned by the creatures.
sentences.i: Rabbi Yose says: Whoever honours the Torah will himself be honoured by people; whoever degrades the Torah will himself be degraded in people's eyes.
sentences.n: גּוּפוֹ, 'his body', is the Mishnaic way of saying 'he himself'. Beside both מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת a later hand wrote in the margin נ״א עַל — 'another copy: עַל' — giving 'honoured above people', the reading of the printed editions.
sentences.say: רַבִּי יוֹסֵה אוֹמֵר כָּל הַמְכַבֵּד אֶת הַתּוֹרָה גוּפוֹ מְכוּבַּד מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת וְכָל הַמְחַלֵּל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה גוּפוֹ מְחוּלָּל מִן הַבְּרִיּוֹת:

sentences.t: ר׳ יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ אוֹמֵ׳ הָחוֹסֵךְ עַצְמוֹ מִן הַדִּין פּוֹרֵק מִמֶּנּוּ אֵיבָה וְגָזֵל וּשְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא וְהַגַּס לִבּוֹ בַהוֹדָיָה שׁוֹטֶה וְרָשָׁע וְגַס רוּחַ
sentences.tr: Rabi Yishma'el bno omer: ha-ḥosekh atsmo min ha-din porek mimenu eiva ve-gazel u-shvu'at shav; ve-ha-gas libo ba-hodaya shote ve-rasha ve-gas ruaḥ.
sentences.l: Rabbi Ishmael his son says: the one-who-holds-back himself from the judgment throws-off from himself enmity and robbery and an oath of vanity; and the one-coarse of his heart in the admission (is) a fool and wicked and coarse of spirit.
sentences.i: His son, Rabbi Ishmael, says: One who keeps himself from sitting in judgment rids himself of enmity, robbery and needless oaths. One who is too proud to concede a point is a fool, a wicked man and an arrogant one.
sentences.n: This Ishmael is the son of R. Yose (4:6). Holding back from judgment means declining to sit as judge, or steering the parties to a compromise. A judge who errs takes one man's property and hands it to another, which is robbery, and the oaths a court imposes may turn out needless or false. Kaufmann reads בַהוֹדָיָה, 'in admission'; the printed editions have בַּהוֹרָאָה, 'in issuing rulings'. Dalet and resh are easily confused, so Kaufmann's word may be a copying slip; taken as written, it describes a man too proud to admit he is wrong. The final kaf of הָחוֹסֵךְ was corrected from a nun.
sentences.say: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ אוֹמֵר הָחוֹסֵךְ עַצְמוֹ מִן הַדִּין פּוֹרֵק מִמֶּנּוּ אֵיבָה וְגָזֵל וּשְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא וְהַגַּס לִבּוֹ בַהוֹדָיָה שׁוֹטֶה וְרָשָׁע וְגַס רוּחַ

sentences.t: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵ׳ אַל תְּהִי דָן יְחִידִי שֶׁאֵין דָּן יָחִיד אֶלָּא אֶחָד וְאַל תֹאמַר קַבְּלוּ דַעְתִּי שֶׁהֶן רַשַּׁיִין וְלֹא אַתָּה:
sentences.tr: Hu haya omer: al tehi dan yeḥidi, she-ein dan yaḥid ela eḥad; ve-al tomar: kablu da'ati, she-hen rashayin ve-lo ata.
sentences.l: He was saying: do not be judging alone, for none judges alone but One; and do not say: accept my opinion — for they are entitled, and not you.
sentences.i: He used to say: Do not sit in judgment alone, for only the One judges alone. And do not say, 'Accept my view,' for the right to decide is theirs, and not yours.
sentences.n: 'The One' is God. רַשַּׁאִין, 'entitled': your colleagues on the bench have the right to decide, and you have no right to impose your view on them. Kaufmann spells it with a double yod, רַשַּׁיִין. Manuscript: the heading הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵ׳ was added in the margin by a second hand; as first written, these words ran straight on from 4:7 as part of R. Ishmael's saying, and 'he' is R. Ishmael in either case. A second hand also added the last yod of יְחִידִי; a yod was erased from קַבְּלוּ; and שֶׁהֶן is written over an erasure.
sentences.say: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר אַל תְּהִי דָן יְחִידִי שֶׁאֵין דָּן יָחִיד אֶלָּא אֶחָד וְאַל תֹאמַר קַבְּלוּ דַעְתִּי שֶׁהֶן רַשַּׁיִין וְלֹא אַתָּה:

sentences.t: ר׳ יוֹנָתָן אוֹמֵ׳ כָּל הַמְקַיֵּים אֶת הַתּוֹרָה מֵעוֹנִי סוֹפוֹ לְקַיְּימָה מֵעוֹשֶׁר וְכָל הַמְבַטֵּל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה מֵעוֹשֶׁר סוֹפוֹ לְבָטְלָה מֵעוֹנִי:
sentences.tr: Rabi Yonatan omer: kol ha-mekayem et ha-tora me-oni sofo lekaymah me-osher, ve-khol ha-mevatel et ha-tora me-osher sofo levatlah me-oni.
sentences.l: Rabbi Jonathan says: whoever fulfils the Torah out of poverty, his end (is) to fulfil it out of wealth; and whoever neglects the Torah out of wealth, his end (is) to neglect it out of poverty.
sentences.i: Rabbi Jonathan says: Whoever keeps the Torah in poverty will in the end keep it in wealth; whoever neglects the Torah in wealth will in the end neglect it in poverty.
sentences.n: מֵעוֹנִי, 'from poverty', means in the midst of poverty, despite it. סוֹפוֹ + infinitive, 'his end is to …', is the Mishnaic way of saying 'he will end up …'; it returns at 4:11. The suffix in לְקַיְּימָה and לְבָטְלָה is 'it' — the Torah, a feminine noun.
sentences.say: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן אוֹמֵר כָּל הַמְקַיֵּים אֶת הַתּוֹרָה מֵעוֹנִי סוֹפוֹ לְקַיְּימָה מֵעוֹשֶׁר וְכָל הַמְבַטֵּל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה מֵעוֹשֶׁר סוֹפוֹ לְבָטְלָה מֵעוֹנִי:

sentences.t: ר׳ מֵאִיר אוֹמֵ׳ הֱוֵוי מְעַט עֵסֶק וַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ בִּפְנֵי כָל הָאָדָם וְאִם בָּטַלְתָּה מִן הַתּוֹרָה יֶשׁ לי בְטֵלִים הַרְבֵּה כְנֶגְדָּךְ וְאִם עָמַלְתָּה בַתּוֹרָה יֶשׁ לי שָׂכָר הַרְבֵּה לִיתֶּן לָךְ:
sentences.tr: Rabi Meir omer: hevei me'at esek va-asok ba-tora, u-shfal ruaḥ bifnei khol ha-adam. Ve-im batalta min ha-tora, yesh li betelim harbe kenegdakh; ve-im amalta ba-tora, yesh li sakhar harbe liten lakh.
sentences.l: Rabbi Meir says: be little of business and occupy-yourself in the Torah, and low of spirit before every person. And if you have been-idle from the Torah, there are for-me idle-things many against you; and if you have toiled in the Torah, there is for-me reward much to give to-you.
sentences.i: Rabbi Meir says: Keep your business small and occupy yourself with Torah, and be humble before everyone. If you neglect the Torah, I have many idle things to set against you; if you labour in the Torah, I have a great reward to give you.
sentences.n: The speaker of the second half is God. בְּטֵלִים, 'idle things', are the distractions and hindrances He sets in the way of one who has abandoned study. Manuscript: in both clauses a later hand corrected לוֹ, 'he has', to לִי, 'I have', so that God speaks in His own voice. The whole second clause, 'and if you have toiled … to give you', was added in the margin. Kaufmann spells the 2ms perfect with a final he: בָּטַלְתָּה, עָמַלְתָּה. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: הַרְבֵּה.
sentences.say: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר הֱוֵוי מְעַט עֵסֶק וַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ בִּפְנֵי כָל הָאָדָם וְאִם בָּטַלְתָּה מִן הַתּוֹרָה יֶשׁ לי בְטֵלִים הַרְבֵּה כְנֶגְדָּךְ וְאִם עָמַלְתָּה בַתּוֹרָה יֶשׁ לי שָׂכָר הַרְבֵּה לִיתֶּן לָךְ:

sentences.t: ר׳ אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹ׳ הָעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה אַחַת קָנָה לוֹ פְּרַקְלִיט אֶחָד הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אַחַת קָנָה לוֹ קָטֵיגוֹר אֶחָד תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים כִּתְרִיס לִפְנֵי הַפּוּרְעָנוּת ר׳ יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדַּלָר אוֹמֵ׳ כָּל כְּנֵסְיָיה שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁום שָׁמַיִם סוֹפָהּ לְהִתְקַיֵּים וְשֶׁאֵינָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם אֵין סוֹפָהּ לְהִיתְקַיֵּים:
sentences.tr: Rabi Eli'ezer ben Ya'akov omer: ha-ose mitsva aḥat kana lo praklit eḥad; ha-over avera aḥat kana lo kategor eḥad. Teshuva u-ma'asim tovim ki-tris lifnei ha-pur'anut. Rabi Yoḥanan ha-Sandalar omer: kol knesiya she-hi le-shem shamayim sofah lehitkayem, ve-she-eina le-shem shamayim ein sofah lehitkayem.
sentences.l: Rabbi Eliezer son of Jacob says: the one-who-does one commandment has acquired for-himself one advocate; the one-who-commits one transgression has acquired for-himself one accuser. Repentance and good deeds (are) like a shield before the punishment. Rabbi Yoḥanan the Sandal-maker says: every assembly that is for the name of Heaven, its end (is) to endure; and (one) that is not for the name of Heaven, its end is not to endure.
sentences.i: Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: One who performs a single commandment gains himself a single advocate; one who commits a single transgression gains himself a single accuser. Repentance and good deeds are a shield against punishment. Rabbi Yoḥanan the Sandal-maker says: Every gathering for the sake of Heaven will endure in the end; a gathering that is not for the sake of Heaven will not endure.
sentences.n: Three words here are Greek borrowings: פְּרַקְלִיט (paraklētos, advocate), קָטֵיגוֹר (katēgoros, accuser) and תְּרִיס (thyreos, a long shield). The heavenly court is pictured as a trial in a Roman-era courtroom. R. Yoḥanan, like many sages, had a trade; Kaufmann vocalizes his title sandalar. לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, 'for the name of Heaven', means for God's sake, with no self-interest; Kaufmann writes the first לְשֵׁם with an extra vav. Manuscript: the final tav of the second אַחַת was corrected from dalet (אֶחָד). Kaufmann begins a new section at R. Yoḥanan. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: קָנָה.
sentences.say: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר הָעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה אַחַת קָנָה לוֹ פְּרַקְלִיט אֶחָד הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אַחַת קָנָה לוֹ קָטֵיגוֹר אֶחָד תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים כִּתְרִיס לִפְנֵי הַפּוּרְעָנוּת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדַּלָר אוֹמֵר כָּל כְּנֵסְיָיה שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁום שָׁמַיִם סוֹפָהּ לְהִתְקַיֵּים וְשֶׁאֵינָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם אֵין סוֹפָהּ לְהִיתְקַיֵּים:

sentences.t: ר׳ אֶלְעָזָר אוֹ׳ יְהִי כְבוֹד תַּלְמִידָךְ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כִכְבוֹד חֲבֵירָךְ וּכְבוֹד חֲבֵירָךְ כְּמוֹרָא רַבָּךְ וּמוֹרָא רַבָּךְ כְּמוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם:
sentences.tr: Rabi Elazar omer: yehi khvod talmidakh ḥaviv alekha ki-khvod ḥaverakh, u-khvod ḥaverakh ke-mora rabakh, u-mora rabakh ke-mora shamayim.
sentences.l: Rabbi Elazar says: let the honour of your student be dear to you like the honour of your fellow, and the honour of your fellow like the fear of your master, and the fear of your master like the fear of Heaven.
sentences.i: Rabbi Elazar says: Let your student's honour be as dear to you as your colleague's; your colleague's honour as the reverence due to your teacher; and the reverence due to your teacher as the reverence due to Heaven.
sentences.n: The printed editions name him R. Elazar ben Shammua and open differently: 'let your student's honour be as dear to you as your own (כְּשֶׁלָּךְ)'. Kaufmann's chain climbs one rung at a time — student, colleague, teacher, Heaven. מוֹרָא is awe, the reverence a student owes his teacher. Note the Mishnaic 2ms suffix -akh throughout: תַּלְמִידָךְ, חֲבֵירָךְ, רַבָּךְ. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: כְבוֹד.
sentences.say: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר יְהִי כְבוֹד תַּלְמִידָךְ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כִכְבוֹד חֲבֵירָךְ וּכְבוֹד חֲבֵירָךְ כְּמוֹרָא רַבָּךְ וּמוֹרָא רַבָּךְ כְּמוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם:

sentences.t: ר׳ יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵ׳ הֱוֵי זָהִיר בַּתַּלְמוּד שֶׁשִׁיגְגַת הַתַּלְמוּד עוֹלָה זָדוֹן ר׳ שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹ׳ שְׁלֹשָׁה כְתָרִים הֵן כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה וְכֶתֶר כְּהוּנָה וְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן:
sentences.tr: Rabi Yehuda omer: hevei zahir ba-talmud, she-shigegat ha-talmud ola zadon. Rabi Shimon omer: shlosha ktarim hen: keter tora, ve-kheter kehuna, ve-kheter malkhut; ve-kheter shem tov al gabeihen.
sentences.l: Rabbi Judah says: be careful in the study, for an error of the study counts-as wilful-sin. Rabbi Simeon says: three crowns there are: the crown of Torah, and the crown of priesthood, and the crown of kingship; and the crown of a good name upon their backs.
sentences.i: Rabbi Judah says: Be careful in your study, for an error in study counts as a deliberate sin. Rabbi Simeon says: There are three crowns — the crown of Torah, the crown of priesthood and the crown of kingship — and the crown of a good name sits above them all.
sentences.n: תַּלְמוּד here is study, especially the learning from which rulings are drawn: a scholar's mistake leads others to sin, so it is treated as wilful. עוֹלָה, 'goes up as', means 'counts as'. The three crowns belong to the scholar, to Aaron's line of priests and to David's line of kings. עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, 'on their backs', means above them. The printed editions read וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, 'rises above them'; Kaufmann has no verb. Manuscript: a second hand corrected ששיגת to שֶׁשִׁיגְגַת, and a doubled וכתר was erased.
sentences.say: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר הֱוֵי זָהִיר בַּתַּלְמוּד שֶׁשִׁיגְגַת הַתַּלְמוּד עוֹלָה זָדוֹן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר שְׁלֹשָׁה כְתָרִים הֵן כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה וְכֶתֶר כְּהוּנָה וְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן:

sentences.t: ר׳ נְהוֹרַיִי אוֹ׳ הֱוֵוי גוֹלֶה לִמְקוֹם תּוֹרָה וְאַל תֹּאמַר הִיא תָבוֹא אַחֲרַיִי שֶׁחֲבֵירֶיךָ יתקַיְּימוּהָ בְיָדֶךָ וְאֶל בִּינָתְךָ אַל תִּישָּׁעֵן
sentences.tr: Rabi Nehoray omer: hevei gole li-mkom tora, ve-al tomar: hi tavo aḥarai, she-ḥaverekha yekaymuha be-yadekha; ve-el binatkha al tisha'en.
sentences.l: Rabbi Nehorai says: be exiling (yourself) to a place of Torah, and do not say: it will come after me — for your companions will make-it-stand in your hand; and on your understanding do not lean.
sentences.i: Rabbi Nehorai says: Go into exile to a place of Torah, and do not say, 'It will follow me,' for it is your companions who will make it secure in your hands. And do not rely on your own understanding.
sentences.n: Exile to a place of Torah means leaving home, if need be, to live among scholars: learning holds fast when companions question and correct you. The last clause is Proverbs 3:5. The printed editions put it as indirect speech, שֶׁהִיא תָבוֹא אַחֲרֶיךָ, 'that it will come after you'; Kaufmann has the speaker's own words, 'after me'. The verb יתקַיְּימוּהָ is odd: the vocalizer pointed only קַיְּימוּהָ (Piel, 'they will make it stand', as in the printed יְקַיְּמוּהָ) and left the first two letters bare; the extra tav may be a slip. The romanization reads the Piel. A second hand added the yod of שֶׁחֲבֵירֶיךָ, making 'your companions' plural, and a vav was erased from תֹּאמַר. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: גוֹלֶה.
sentences.say: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַיִי אוֹמֵר הֱוֵוי גוֹלֶה לִמְקוֹם תּוֹרָה וְאַל תֹּאמַר הִיא תָבוֹא אַחֲרַיִי שֶׁחֲבֵירֶיךָ יתקַיְּימוּהָ בְיָדֶךָ וְאֶל בִּינָתְךָ אַל תִּישָּׁעֵן

sentences.t: ר׳ יַנַּיִי אוֹ׳ אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ לֹא מִשַּׁלְוַות הָרְשָׁעִים וְלֹא מִיִּסּוּרֵיהֶן שֶׁלַצַּדִּיקִים: מַתְּתְיָה בֶן חָרָשׁ אוֹ׳ הֱוֵוי מַקְדִּים לִשְׁלוֹם כָּל הָאָדָם וֶהֱוֵוי זָנָב לָאֲרָיוֹת וְלֹא רֹאשׁ לַשּׁוּעָלִים:
sentences.tr: Rabi Yanay omer: ein be-yadeinu lo mi-shalvat ha-resha'im ve-lo mi-yisureihen shela-tsadikim. Matetya ben Ḥarash omer: hevei makdim li-shlom kol ha-adam, ve-hevei zanav la-arayot ve-lo rosh la-shu'alim.
sentences.l: Rabbi Yannai says: there is not in our hands (anything) — neither of the ease of the wicked, nor of the sufferings of the righteous. Mattetya son of Ḥarash says: be first to the greeting of every person; and be a tail to the lions and not a head to the foxes.
sentences.i: Rabbi Yannai says: We have no grasp of why the wicked live at ease, nor of why the righteous suffer. Mattetya ben Ḥarash says: Be the first to greet everyone. And be a tail to lions rather than a head to foxes.
sentences.n: אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ, 'it is not in our hands': we can explain neither the ease of the wicked nor the sufferings of the righteous. The printed editions read וְאַף לֹא, 'nor even'; Kaufmann's וְלֹא is written over an erasure. Mattetya ben Ḥarash (printed מַתְיָא) taught in Rome in the second century. 'A tail to lions': better to follow among the great than to lead among the petty. Kaufmann runs R. Yannai's saying on from 4:14 and begins a new section at Mattetya. A lamed was erased before כָּל. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: מַתְּתְיָה.
sentences.say: רַבִּי יַנַּיִי אוֹמֵר אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ לֹא מִשַּׁלְוַות הָרְשָׁעִים וְלֹא מִיִּסּוּרֵיהֶן שֶׁלַצַּדִּיקִים: מַתְּתְיָה בֶן חָרָשׁ אוֹמֵר הֱוֵוי מַקְדִּים לִשְׁלוֹם כָּל הָאָדָם וֶהֱוֵוי זָנָב לָאֲרָיוֹת וְלֹא רֹאשׁ לַשּׁוּעָלִים:

sentences.t: ר׳ עֲקִיבָה אוֹ׳ הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דּוֹמֶה לִפְרוֹזְדּוֹר לִפְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא הַתְקֵן עַצְמָךְ לִפְרוֹזְדּוֹר כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּיכָּנֵס לִיטְרִיקְלִין
sentences.tr: Rabi Akiva omer: ha-olam ha-ze dome li-prozdor lifnei ha-olam ha-ba. Hatken atsmakh li-prozdor kedei she-tikanes li-triklin.
sentences.l: Rabbi Akiva says: this world is like a vestibule before the world to come; prepare yourself at the vestibule, so that you may enter the banquet-hall.
sentences.i: Rabbi Akiva says: This world is like an entrance hall before the world to come. Make yourself ready in the entrance hall, so that you may enter the banqueting hall.
sentences.n: Both nouns are Greek loanwords: פְּרוֹזְדּוֹר (prothyron, the porch in front of a door) and טְרַקְלִין (triklinion, the dining room where guests reclined at a feast). The printed editions give this saying to R. Jacob (רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב); Kaufmann names R. Akiva, spelled with a final he. Manuscript: כְּדֵי was added in the margin, and in both occurrences of פְּרוֹזְדּוֹר the final resh was corrected from dalet, or the reverse — the transcriber cannot tell which. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: לִפְרוֹזְדּוֹר.
sentences.say: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָה אוֹמֵר הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דּוֹמֶה לִפְרוֹזְדּוֹר לִפְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא הַתְקֵן עַצְמָךְ לִפְרוֹזְדּוֹר כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּיכָּנֵס לִיטְרִיקְלִין

sentences.t: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵ׳ יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּבְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִכָּל חַיֵּי הַעוֹלָם הַבָּא יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת שֶׁלְקוֹרַת רוּחַ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא מִכָּל חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
sentences.tr: Hu haya omer: yafa sha'a aḥat bi-tshuva u-ve-ma'asim tovim ba-olam ha-ze mi-kol ḥayei ha-olam ha-ba; yafa sha'a aḥat shel korat ruaḥ ba-olam ha-ba mi-kol ḥayei ha-olam ha-ze.
sentences.l: He was saying: fair (is) one hour in repentance and in good deeds in this world from all the life of the world to come; fair (is) one hour of coolness of spirit in the world to come from all the life of this world.
sentences.i: He used to say: Better one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than the whole life of the world to come; and better one hour of serene contentment in the world to come than the whole life of this world.
sentences.n: יָפֶה … מִ…, 'fair … from', is the Mishnaic comparative, 'better than'. In this world a person can still act and change; in the next he can only receive. קוֹרַת רוּחַ, 'coolness of spirit', is contentment, ease of mind. 'He' is the sage of 4:16 — in Kaufmann, R. Akiva; Kaufmann runs this saying on without a break. Manuscript: the first מִכָּל was added in the margin.
sentences.say: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּבְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִכָּל חַיֵּי הַעוֹלָם הַבָּא יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת שֶׁלְקוֹרַת רוּחַ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא מִכָּל חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

sentences.t: ר׳ שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹ׳ אַל תְּרַצֵּה אֶת חֲבֵירָךְ בְּשָׁעַת כַּעסוֹ וְאַל תְּנַחֲמֶנּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמֵּתוֹ מוּטַל לְפָנָיו וְאַל תִּשְׁאַל לוֹ בְּשַׁעַת נִדְרוֹ וְאַל תִּשְׁתַּדֵּל לִרְאוֹתוֹ בְשָׁעַת קַלְקַלָתוֹ:
sentences.tr: Rabi Shimon omer: al teratse et ḥaverakh be-sha'at ka'aso, ve-al tenaḥamenu be-sha'a she-meto mutal lefanav, ve-al tish'al lo be-sha'at nidro, ve-al tishtadel lir'oto be-sha'at kalkalato.
sentences.l: Rabbi Simeon says: do not appease your fellow in the hour of his anger, and do not comfort him in the hour that his dead (one) lies before him, and do not ask for-him in the hour of his vow, and do not try to see him in the hour of his disgrace.
sentences.i: Rabbi Simeon says: Do not try to calm your friend while he is angry, or comfort him while his dead still lies before him. Do not seek release from his vow at the moment he makes it, and do not try to see him in his hour of disgrace.
sentences.n: Each clause warns against the right deed at the wrong moment. שָׁאַל לוֹ, 'ask for him', refers to annulling a vow: a sage could release a person from a rash vow by asking whether he would have made it had he foreseen the outcome — asked in the heat of the moment, he will only insist on it. קַלְקָלָה is disgrace or downfall: a man caught in a wrong wants no witnesses. The printed editions name him R. Simeon ben Elazar. Manuscript: the final he of בּשָׁעָה was corrected from tav; the second half of תִּשְׁתַּדֵּל is a correction; the last vav of לִרְאוֹתו was added by a second hand. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: בְּשָׁעָה, לִרְאוֹתוֹ.
sentences.say: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר אַל תְּרַצֵּה אֶת חֲבֵירָךְ בְּשָׁעַת כַּעסוֹ וְאַל תְּנַחֲמֶנּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמֵּתוֹ מוּטַל לְפָנָיו וְאַל תִּשְׁאַל לוֹ בְּשַׁעַת נִדְרוֹ וְאַל תִּשְׁתַּדֵּל לִרְאוֹתוֹ בְשָׁעַת קַלְקַלָתוֹ:

sentences.t: שְמוּאֵ׳ הַקָּטָן אוֹמ׳ בִּנְפוֹל אוֹיְבְךָ אַל תִּשְׂמַח וּבְהִכָּשְׁלוֹ אַל יָגֵל לִבֶּךָ:
sentences.tr: Shmu'el ha-katan omer: binfol oyivkha al tismaḥ, u-ve-hikashlo al yagel libekha.
sentences.l: Samuel the Small says: in the falling of your enemy do not rejoice, and in his stumbling let your heart not exult.
sentences.i: Samuel the Small says: 'When your enemy falls, do not rejoice; when he stumbles, let your heart not be glad.'
sentences.n: Samuel the Small's whole saying is a verse, Proverbs 24:17, quoted with no introduction and no comment. The printed editions continue with the next verse (24:18): 'lest the LORD see it and be displeased, and turn His anger away from him'. Kaufmann stops at the end of 24:17. Samuel, a sage of Yavne, was said to have been called 'the Small' for his humility.
sentences.say: שְׁמוּאֵל הַקָּטָן אוֹמֵר בִּנְפוֹל אוֹיְבְךָ אַל תִּשְׂמַח וּבְהִכָּשְׁלוֹ אַל יָגֵל לִבֶּךָ:

sentences.t: אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן אֲבִייָּה אוֹ׳ הַלָּמֵד יֶלֶד לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לִדְיוֹ כְתוּבָה עַל נְיָיר חָדָשׁ הַלָּמֵד זָקֵן לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לִדְיוֹ כְתוּבָה עַל נְיָיר מָחוּק: ר׳ יוֹסֵה בֶן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר הַבַּבְלִי אוֹמֵ׳ הַלָּמֵד מִן הַקְּטָנִים לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לְאוֹכֵל עֲנָבִים קֵיהוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן מִגִּיתּוֹ וְהַלָּמֵד מִן הַזְּקֵנִים לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לְאֹכֵל עֲנָבִים בְּשֵׁילוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן יָשָׁן: ר׳ מֵאִיר אוֹמֵ׳ אַל תִּיסְתַּכֵּל בַּקִּינְקֵן אֶלָּא בְּמָה שֶׁיֶּש בּוֹ יֵש קִינְקֵן חָדָשׁ מָלֵא יַיִן יָשָׁן וְיָשָׁן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ חָדָשׁ אֵין בּוֹ
sentences.tr: Elisha ben Aviya omer: ha-lamed yeled, le-ma hu dome? Li-dyo ktuva al niyar ḥadash. Ha-lamed zaken, le-ma hu dome? Li-dyo ktuva al niyar maḥuk. Rabi Yose ben Yehuda ish Kfar ha-Bavli omer: ha-lamed min ha-ktanim, le-ma hu dome? Le-okhel anavim kehot ve-shote yayin mi-gito. Ve-ha-lamed min ha-zkenim, le-ma hu dome? Le-okhel anavim beshelot ve-shote yayin yashan. Rabi Meir omer: al tistakel ba-kinkan ela be-ma she-yesh bo: yesh kinkan ḥadash male yayin yashan, ve-yashan she-afilu ḥadash ein bo.
sentences.l: Elisha son of Aviya says: the one-who-learns (as) a child — to what is he like? To ink written on new paper. The one-who-learns (as) an old-man — to what is he like? To ink written on erased paper. Rabbi Yose son of Judah man of Kefar ha-Bavli says: the one-who-learns from the young — to what is he like? To one-who-eats grapes (that are) sour and drinks wine from its vat. And the one-who-learns from the old — to what is he like? To one-who-eats grapes (that are) ripe and drinks wine (that is) old. Rabbi Meir says: do not look at the jug but at what there is in it: there is a new jug full of old wine, and an old (one) that even new (wine) is not in it.
sentences.i: Elisha ben Aviya says: One who learns as a child — what is he like? Ink written on fresh paper. One who learns as an old man — what is he like? Ink written on paper scraped clean. Rabbi Yose ben Judah of Kefar ha-Bavli says: One who learns from the young — what is he like? One who eats unripe grapes and drinks wine straight from the vat. One who learns from the old — what is he like? One who eats ripe grapes and drinks aged wine. Rabbi Meir says: Do not look at the jug; look at what is in it. There is a new jug full of old wine, and an old jug with not even new wine in it.
sentences.n: Elisha ben Avuya (so the printed editions; Kaufmann אֲבִייָּה) was R. Meir's teacher and the most famous heretic of rabbinic literature, called אַחֵר, 'the Other'. Erased paper is a sheet scraped for reuse, where new ink blurs and the old writing shows through. לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה, 'to what is he like?', is the standard opening of a rabbinic comparison. קֵהוֹת are sour grapes that set the teeth on edge; wine from the vat is still raw. R. Meir's saying reads as a reply to R. Yose: a young teacher can hold old wisdom. Kaufmann spells the jug קִינְקֵן (printed קַנְקַן) and begins new sections at R. Yose and at R. Meir. Manuscript: the first לִדְיוֹ is written by a second hand over an erasure, and לִדְיוֹ כְתוּבָה in the second comparison was added in the margin; both וְשׁוֹתֶה were corrected from lamed; an alef was erased before R. Yose. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: דוֹמֶה, יוֹסֵה.
sentences.say: אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן אֲבִייָּה אוֹמֵר הַלָּמֵד יֶלֶד לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לִדְיוֹ כְתוּבָה עַל נְיָיר חָדָשׁ הַלָּמֵד זָקֵן לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לִדְיוֹ כְתוּבָה עַל נְיָיר מָחוּק: רַבִּי יוֹסֵה בֶן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר הַבַּבְלִי אוֹמֵר הַלָּמֵד מִן הַקְּטָנִים לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לְאוֹכֵל עֲנָבִים קֵיהוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן מִגִּיתּוֹ וְהַלָּמֵד מִן הַזְּקֵנִים לְמָה הוּא דוֹמֶה לְאֹכֵל עֲנָבִים בְּשֵׁילוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן יָשָׁן: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר אַל תִּיסְתַּכֵּל בַּקִּינְקֵן אֶלָּא בְּמָה שֶׁיֶּש בּוֹ יֵש קִינְקֵן חָדָשׁ מָלֵא יַיִן יָשָׁן וְיָשָׁן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ חָדָשׁ אֵין בּוֹ

sentences.t: ר׳ אֶלְעָזָר הַכַּפָּר אוֹמֵ׳ הַקִּינְאָה וְהַתַּאֲוָה וְהַכָּבוֹד מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם:
sentences.tr: Rabi Elazar ha-Kapar omer: ha-kin'a ve-ha-ta'ava ve-ha-kavod motsi'in et ha-adam min ha-olam.
sentences.l: Rabbi Elazar ha-Kappar says: the envy and the desire and the honour take-out the person from the world.
sentences.i: Rabbi Elazar ha-Kappar says: Envy, lust and the pursuit of honour drive a person out of the world.
sentences.n: 'Out of the world' can mean out of this life before his time, or out of the world to come. Manuscript: the title ר׳ was added in the margin, and a yod was erased from the name — the scribe first wrote אליעזר, Eliezer. In Kaufmann this saying runs on from R. Meir's in 4:20 without a break. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: הָעוֹלָם.
sentences.say: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַכַּפָּר אוֹמֵר הַקִּינְאָה וְהַתַּאֲוָה וְהַכָּבוֹד מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם:

sentences.t: הוּא הָיָה אוֹ׳ הַיִּלּוֹדִים לָמוּת וְהַמֵּתִים לִחְיוֹת וְהַחַיִּים לִידּוֹן לֵידָע וּלְהוֹדִיַע וּלְהִיוָּודַע שֶׁהוּא הַיּוֹצֵר וְהוּא הַבּוֹרֵא הוּא הַמֵּבִין וְהוּא הַדַּיָּין הוּא עֵד הוּא בַעַל דִּין וְהוּא עָתִיד לָדוֹן שֶׁאֵין לְפָנָיו לֹא עַוְלָה וְלֹא שִׁכְחָה וְלֹא מְשׂוֹא פָנִים וְלֹא מַקַּח שֹׁחַד שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ וְדַע שֶׁהַכֹּל בְחֶשְׁבּוֹן וְאַל יַבְטִיחָךְ יִצְרָךְ שֶׁהַשְּׁאוֹל בֵּית מָנוֹס שֶׁעַל כָּרְחָךְ אַתָּה נוֹצָר וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ אַתָּה נוֹלַד וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ אַתָּ׳ חַיִ וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ אַתָּ׳ מֵת וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ אַתָּה עָתִיד לִיתֶּן דִּין וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּבָּ״הֻ:
sentences.tr: Hu haya omer: ha-yilodim lamut, ve-ha-metim liḥyot, ve-ha-ḥayim lidon, leida u-lehodia u-lehivada she-hu ha-yotser, ve-hu ha-bore, hu ha-mevin, ve-hu ha-dayan, hu ed, hu ba'al din, ve-hu atid ladun; she-ein lefanav lo avla, ve-lo shikhḥa, ve-lo maso fanim, ve-lo makaḥ shoḥad, she-ha-kol shelo. Ve-da she-ha-kol be-ḥeshbon, ve-al yavtiḥakh yitsrakh she-ha-she'ol beit manos; she-al korḥakh ata notsar, ve-al korḥakh ata nolad, ve-al korḥakh ata ḥai, ve-al korḥakh ata met, ve-al korḥakh ata atid liten din ve-ḥeshbon lifnei melekh malkhei ha-mlakhim, ha-Kadosh barukh hu.
sentences.l: He was saying: the born (are) to die, and the dead to live, and the living to be-judged — to know, and to make-known, and to be-made-known that He is the Former, and He is the Creator, He is the Discerner, and He is the Judge, He is witness, He is party-to-the-case, and He is destined to judge; for there is not before Him wrongdoing, and not forgetting, and not lifting of face, and not taking of bribe, for everything is His. And know that everything (is) by reckoning; and let your inclination not assure you that the grave (is) a house of refuge; for against your will you are formed, and against your will you are born, and against your will you live, and against your will you die, and against your will you are destined to give judgment and reckoning before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
sentences.i: He used to say: Those who are born will die, the dead will live again, and the living will be judged — so that they may know, make known and come to know that He is the Maker, He the Creator, He the Discerner, He the Judge, He the Witness, He the Plaintiff, and He will judge in time to come. With Him there is no injustice, no forgetting, no favouritism and no taking of bribes, for everything is His. Know that everything is reckoned. Do not let your impulse assure you that the grave will be a refuge: against your will you were formed, against your will you were born, against your will you live, against your will you die, and against your will you will one day render a full account before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
sentences.n: 'He' is R. Elazar ha-Kappar (4:21). מַשּׂוֹא פָנִים, 'lifting of face', is the biblical idiom for favouritism: showing regard to a litigant for who he is. בַּעַל דִּין, 'owner of a case', is a party to a lawsuit — here the one who brings the charge. שְׁאוֹל, Sheol, is the biblical underworld; בֵּית מָנוֹס, 'a house of escape'. עַל כָּרְחָךְ, 'against your will', is a fixed Mishnaic phrase; in all five occurrences the scribe first wrote כורחך and the vav was erased. Persian kings styled themselves 'king of kings'; God is King over those kings. The printed editions add בָּרוּךְ הוּא before שֶׁאֵין לְפָנָיו, read לְפִי הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן, 'according to the reckoning', and add לָךְ, 'a refuge for you'. The vav of וּלְהוֹדִיַע was added by a second hand. The last word is the abbreviation הקב״ה, 'the Holy One, blessed be He'.
